title: Scrapstorm
hook: A tiny magnetic robot turns loose rubbish into an orbiting shield, then throws that protection away as its main attack.
audience: Players of compact arena action roguelites who enjoy readable risk, aiming and build combinations.
core_loop: Position against biters and telegraphed shooters; hold a finite scrap ring as protection or launch its held pieces; recover globally in motion and choose whether to fire a partial ring; select two early upgrades across four cleared encounters; defeat the finale and retry. A 5-7-minute run is a tuning target, not a minimum duration.
score_notes: Demand: paid genre supported, our product untested. Distinctiveness: protection sacrificed to attack, contingent on meaningful choice. Fun: no build. Scope: balance/content and readability could exceed seven days. Distribution: a short gather-throw-recover clip is legible; reach unmeasured.
design_stage: Detailed exploration requested by owner; no prototype or production selection.

inspiration.topic: Miniatures made from discarded materials and upcycling
inspiration.connection: The trend inspires the toy-scale world, found-object weapons and making discarded parts useful. The game is arena combat, not a craft simulator.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: The shield-versus-attack decision and recoveries should remain enjoyable without interest in upcycling.
inspiration.current_timing: Historical source growth or current expansion is recorded separately; September search slope and future peak are unverified.

commercial_hypothesis.condition: Genre/price evidence and a worthwhile finished experience within the work budget are both required. These are test prices, not selected prices or sales forecasts.
commercial_hypothesis.higher_price_condition: USD 6.99 can be reconsidered only after observed replay depth and presentation justify it; do not add scope solely to reach a price.

prototype_envelope.scope: One-day three-minute arena with two complementary enemies, six conserved pieces, deterministic shielding, aimed launch, global recall at full movement speed, partial recovery, death and instant retry. First test without progression; compare one early Return Teeth toggle if harmless recall feels like reload work.

production_envelope.scope: One 2D arena and robot, four bounded encounters, two ordinary enemy types plus a simple finale, six conserved scrap pieces, six upgrade definitions with two selected per run, local records/save and a packaged Windows build. A harder preset is cuttable; typical 5-7-minute run length is unproved and must not be padded.
cuts: Three arena variants in the first product
Twelve to sixteen upgrades in the first product
Five upgrade picks that make small-pool builds converge
Limited-radius recall and compulsory movement slowdown
Passive damage from orbiting or blocking
production_envelope.note: Includes prototype, original modest art/audio, finite content, controls/settings/save, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Calendar onboarding/review, recruitment and unforeseen rework are separate. Estimate is not demonstrated.

cash_assumptions.note: Existing tools assumed. No purchases or cash allocation. Steam fee and optional assets remain separate planning inputs in the run.

support_estimate: Allow 1–2 owner hours for launch-month triage/review, plus agent fixes as needed; actual burden unknown.

evidence.claim: Published August 25, 2026: miniatures from trash searches +437%, global text searches May 2026 versus May 2025. This supplies inspiration, not September acceleration or game purchase intent.
Brotato: USD 4.99 regular / 2.99 current, 110,928 all-language Steam-purchase reviews in the dated snapshot. Arena action and upgrade reference, not our achievable content inventory.

April 26, 2023 Blobfish/Seaven press release reproduced by Nintendo-Town reports Brotato sold over 1.5 million copies. Platform split and realized purchase prices not supplied; this is a reported disclosure, not an independently audited total.
SNKRX: USD 2.99 regular/current and 4,197 consistently filtered reviews. Compact arena/build reference; no primary paid-unit total found.
Spreadsheet Survivors launched July 31, 2026 and has two Steam-purchase reviews in this run. A distinctive thematic wrapper in this genre does not ensure visibility.
Spellbound Survivors supplies another lower-response arena action comparator; prices and review totals are saved in steam-arena-counterexamples.json.

risks: Genre incumbents offer much more content below USD 5.
Orbiting weapons alone are familiar; an active sacrifice-and-retrieve decision must matter.
Scrap collection may be busywork; unrestricted physics would exceed the budget.
The physical miniature audience may not want a digital combat game.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No own playable build, competitor hands-on test, measured organic conversion, target-player willingness to pay or validated production time. Current names are working titles without clearance.
next_test: Use the one-day combat slice before progression. With five available players, seek four who explain protection/ammunition, three who deliberately vary launch or recovery and three who voluntarily retry. Ask which moment they want again and which action feels like work. Compare harmless recall with a bounded return-damage toggle; if that supplies the enjoyment, revise the core rather than locking it behind progression. Hold or redesign if both remain rote or frustrating after a focused tuning pass. No fun or price-value claim follows from designer agreement.
decision_reason: Owner requested detailed exploration and two designers discussing improvements. Their exchange produced a concrete 17-point brief and a smaller run with more deliberate recovery choices. The concept remains shortlisted; fun, sufficient commercial replay and the production estimate are unproved.

decision_history.reason: First recommended experiment for an active, immediately visible hook and strong paid genre evidence. Trend-to-buyer transfer, fun and production duration remain unproved. Research only; no game selected.

Detailed design exploration after an explicit two-designer exchange. Conserved ammo, global full-speed recall, partial volleys, four encounters and two choices from six upgrades replace the larger initial outline. Prototype and production are not selected.

independent_challenge: On September 7, two game designers directly exchanged a proposal, challenge and revision. They removed recall chores, shield-gap randomness, passive block damage and a guaranteed retained-shield upgrade. Both retained the objection that the game may be a gun with an annoying reload and that a short run with two enemy types has unproven commercial depth. Return-path damage is an early comparative experiment, not an established fun result.
